note: Evidence: Apple Music catalogue (iTunes Search/Lookup API) track lists and IMSLP api.php work info. Decisions to confirm: (1) Purcell's sonatas of 1683 and 1697 are entered as four parts (two violins, bass violin or bass viol, continuo), as IMSLP's collection page and the 1683 title give them; the census single pages say three. (2) Pavans Z. 748–751 entered as two violins and continuo (Musica Amphion's titles), the four-part Pavan Z. 752 and the Overtures Z. 771–772 as strings alone like the Chacony benchmark; the overtures (one recording, Musica Amphion) are medium confidence and may be band music. (3) Jacquet de La Guerre's 1707 sonatas left as duos although La Rêveuse records three with 'viole obligée'; the two Brossard manuscript sonatas whose title names an obbligato viol were added. (4) Marais's 1723 pieces entered with continuo (the harpsichord realises the bass), Rameau's concerts with obbligato harpsichord (derived formation 'other').
